deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the Dataproc Session Template can be destroyed or removed from Terraform management. Preventing unintended deletion can protect resource availability and prevent destructive loss.

labels.description:
The labels to associate with this session template.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are descriptive key-value metadata used to organize resources. They do not directly control access, identity, encryption, networking, or other security controls.

location.description: The location in which the session template will be created in.
location.rationale: Determines the region where the Dataproc Session Template is created. Restricting deployment to approved regions supports data residency and platform security requirements.

name.description:
The resource name of the session template in the following format:
projects/{project}/locations/{location}/sessionTemplates/{template_id}
name.rationale: Identifies the Dataproc Session Template resource but does not directly control access, identity, encryption, networking, or other security settings.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project that owns the resource. It is a resource reference and does not directly configure the resource's security controls.

environment_config.description: Environment configuration for the session execution.

environment_config.execution_config.idle.description:
The duration to keep the session alive while it's idling.
Exceeding this threshold causes the session to terminate. Minimum value is 10 minutes; maximum value is 14 day.
Defaults to 1 hour if not set. If both ttl and idleTtl are specified for an interactive session, the conditions
are treated as OR conditions: the workload will be terminated when it has been idle for idleTtl or when ttl has
been exceeded, whichever occurs first.
environment_config.execution_config.idle.rationale: Controls how long an idle session can remain active before termination. It affects session lifetime but does not directly control access, identity, encryption, or networking.

environment_config.execution_config.kms_.description: The Cloud KMS key to use for encryption.
environment_config.execution_config.kms_.rationale: Controls the Cloud KMS key used to encrypt the workload. The selected encryption key directly affects protection of workload data.

environment_config.execution_config.netw.description: Tags used for network traffic control.
environment_config.execution_config.netw.rationale: Network tags associate the workload with network traffic-control rules. Their selection is a team architectural choice rather than a platform security policy target.

environment_config.execution_config.serv.description: Service account that used to execute workload.
environment_config.execution_config.serv.rationale: Controls the identity used by the workload. The service account determines the permissions available to the workload and therefore directly affects access control.

environment_config.execution_config.stag.description:
A Cloud Storage bucket used to stage workload dependencies, config files, and store
workload output and other ephemeral data, such as Spark history files. If you do not specify a staging bucket,
Cloud Dataproc will determine a Cloud Storage location according to the region where your workload is running,
and then create and manage project-level, per-location staging and temporary buckets.
This field requires a Cloud Storage bucket name, not a gs://... URI to a Cloud Storage bucket.
environment_config.execution_config.stag.rationale: Specifies the Cloud Storage bucket used to stage workload dependencies, configuration, output, and ephemeral data. The selected bucket can therefore affect protection of workload data.

environment_config.execution_config.subn.rationale: References the subnetwork used for workload execution. It identifies a network resource but is not itself a platform security policy target.

environment_config.execution_config.ttl.description:
The duration after which the workload will be terminated.
When the workload exceeds this duration, it will be unconditionally terminated without waiting for ongoing
work to finish. If ttl is not specified for a session workload, the workload will be allowed to run until it
exits naturally (or run forever without exiting). If ttl is not specified for an interactive session,
it defaults to 24 hours. If ttl is not specified for a batch that uses 2.1+ runtime version, it defaults to 4 hours.
Minimum value is 10 minutes; maximum value is 14 days. If both ttl and idleTtl are specified (for an interactive session),
the conditions are treated as OR conditions: the workload will be terminated when it has been idle for idleTtl or
when ttl has been exceeded, whichever occurs first.
environment_config.execution_config.ttl.rationale: Controls the maximum workload lifetime but does not directly configure access, identity, encryption, or network security.

environment_config.execution_config.auth.description: Authentication configuration for a workload is used to set the default identity for the workload execution.
Authentication type for the user workload running in containers. Possible values: ["SERVICE_ACCOUNT", "END_USER_CREDENTIALS"]
environment_config.execution_config.auth.rationale: Controls how the user workload authenticates during execution. The authentication method directly affects workload identity and access control.

environment_config.peripherals_config.description: Peripherals configuration that workload has access to.

environment_config.peripherals_config.me.description: Resource name of an existing Dataproc Metastore service.
environment_config.peripherals_config.me.rationale: Identifies an existing Dataproc Metastore service available to the workload but does not directly configure its access or security controls.

environment_config.peripherals_config.sp.description: The Spark History Server configuration for the workload.
Resource name of an existing Dataproc Cluster to act as a Spark History Server for the workload.
environment_config.peripherals_config.sp.rationale: Identifies the Dataproc cluster used for Spark History Server functionality but does not directly configure security controls for the workload.

jupyter_session.description: Jupyter configuration for an interactive session.

jupyter_session.display_name.description: Display name, shown in the Jupyter kernelspec card.
jupyter_session.display_name.rationale: Controls only the name displayed for the Jupyter session and does not directly affect access, identity, encryption, networking, or data protection.

jupyter_session.kernel.description: Kernel to be used with Jupyter interactive session. Possible values: ["PYTHON", "SCALA"]
jupyter_session.kernel.rationale: Selects the Jupyter kernel used by the session. It determines the execution language but does not directly configure access, identity, encryption, or networking.

runtime_config.description: Runtime configuration for the session template.

runtime_config.container_image.description: Optional custom container image for the job runtime environment. If not specified, a default container image will be used.
runtime_config.container_image.rationale: Controls the container image used for the workload runtime. The image determines the software and dependencies executed by the workload and can therefore affect security.

runtime_config.properties.description: A mapping of property names to values, which are used to configure workload execution.
runtime_config.properties.rationale: Runtime properties can change workload execution behavior, including settings that can affect security and data handling.

runtime_config.version.rationale: Determines the runtime software environment used by the workload. Restricting runtime versions can help prevent use of unsupported or vulnerable software environments.

spark_connect_session.description: Spark connect configuration for an interactive session.
